rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted object makes the command exclusive by reversal: it answers idolaters who worship only their own gods, rather than adding Allah to a set of gods they worship.
rows.anchor: والجملة تفيد الحصر بتقديم المفعول على سبيل الاشتغال، و القصر قصر قلب لا قصر إفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists said Allah cannot be encompassed by knowledge or understanding, so they turned to angels and exemplary humans or jinn as powerful intermediaries whose worship secures benefit and averts harm.
rows.anchor: معتذرين بأن الله سبحانه لا يحيط به علم ولا يناله فهم فلا يمكن التوجه إليه بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear Allah is a metonym for worship; the intended fear is reverential awe, not fear of punishment, matching the earlier account of angels’ fear as the origin of worship’s legislation.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالرهبة كناية عن الأمر بالعبادة وإنما اختصت الرهبة بالذكر

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon defines waṣb as an abiding sickness; in the verse, waṣiban means lasting, and the phrase warns that the penalty for adopting two gods is severe and inescapable.
rows.anchor: الوصب السقم اللازم وقد وصب فلان فهو وصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here dīn means obedience, and waṣiban means perpetual: a person should obey Allah in every state, as the angels do without disobeying His commands.
rows.anchor: ويكون الدين ههنا الطاعة، ومعنى الواصب الدائم أي حق الإنسان أن يطيعه دائما

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon also gives related usages: waṣaba means to last, waṣaba al-dīn means to become obligatory, and a waṣiba desert is distant without end.
rows.anchor: ويقال وصب وصوبا دام، ووصب الدين وجب، ومفازة واصبة بعيدة لا غاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth truly belongs to Allah: its attributes and acts depend on Him for existence and manifestation and cannot be severed from Him even momentarily, like a person’s hearing and sight belonging to that person.
rows.anchor: الأشياء قائمة به قيام الملك بمالكه مملوكة له ملكا حقيقيا لا يقبل تغييرا ولا انتقالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Allah truly owns everything, He alone manages it; the manager is its Lord, and therefore only He should be feared and worshipped.
rows.anchor: كان هو تعالى المدبر لأمر العالم إذ لا معنى لكون العالم مملوكا له بهذا الملك ثم يستقل غيره بتدبير أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Lord, Allah must establish the human way of life that leads people to their proper end and happiness; the Quran calls this way dīn, so Allah alone owns and legislates religion.
rows.anchor: وهذه السنة والطريقة هي التي يسميها القرآن دينا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes dīn here to mean obedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالدين الطاعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes dīn here to mean kingship or sovereignty.
rows.anchor: وقيل الملك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reported interpretation takes dīn here to mean recompense.
rows.anchor: وقيل الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers dīn as the divinely legislated way of life because it best fits the surrounding discussion of Allah’s lordship and the revelation of religion through prophecy.
rows.anchor: والأوجه هو ما قدمناه لأنه أوفق وأنسب بسياق ما يحفها من الآيات السابقة واللاحقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks rhetorically whether anyone but Allah should be feared and worshipped: no other being owns or manages anything or has the right to legislate a religion.
rows.anchor: فهل غيره تعالى تتقون وتعبدون؟ وليس يملك شيئا ولا يدبر أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that every blessing comes from Allah supplies another proof of His exclusive lordship and rebukes people for associating partners and inventing religious rules without His permission.
rows.anchor: بيان آخر لوحدانيته تعالى في الربوبية يفرع سبحانه عليه ذمهم وتوبيخهم على شركهم بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḍurr means a bad condition caused by losing a blessing that sustains well-being; al-juʾār is the call of wild animals, used figuratively for raising one’s voice in supplication and distress.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالضر سوء الحال من جهة فقدان النعمة التي تصلح بها الحال، والجؤار بضم الجيم صوت الوحوش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal claim that blessings come from Allah is already established by the preceding verses and accepted by the audience; when distress removes even a small blessing, they cry to Allah alone, proving He gives blessings and removes harm.
rows.anchor: وأنتم تعلمون ذلك ثم إذا حل بكم شيء من الضر وسوء حال يسير رفعتم أصواتكم بالتضرع وجأرتم إليه لا إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People’s instinctive appeal to Allah in disasters is necessary evidence: even an unbeliever does not lose hope in extreme hardship, and hope or any relation such as desire requires an existing object or counterpart.
rows.anchor: فمن الضروري أن تحقق ما لا يخلو من معنى التعلق كالحب والبغض والإرادة والكراهة والجذب ونظائرها في الخارج

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon explains that Abraham was an ummah because he stood in worship as a whole community would, like saying that one person is a tribe.
rows.anchor: أي قائما مقام جماعة في عبادة الله نحو قولهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A view attributed to Ibn Abbas is close to the lexicon’s explanation that Abraham was a community in himself.
rows.anchor: وهو قريب مما نقل عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation understands ummah as an imam whom people follow.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه الإمام المقتدى به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation says Abraham was for a time the only monotheist on earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه كان أمة منحصرة في واحد مدة من الزمان لم يكن على الأرض موحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunūt means obedience and worship, or their continuance; ḥanīf means turning from either extreme toward the balanced middle.
rows.anchor: القنوت الإطاعة والعبادة أو دوامها، والحنف الميل من الطرفين إلى حاق الوسط وهو الإعتدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtibāʾ derives from gathering: Allah’s choosing a person means reserving him for Himself and gathering him out of dispersion among divergent creeds.
rows.anchor: الاجتباء من الجباية وهو الجمع واجتباء الله الإنسان هو إخلاصه لنفسه وجمعه من التفرق في المذاهب المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause after Abraham is described as grateful and before Allah chose him signals that gratitude causes divine choosing; this supports the earlier view that true gratitude is exclusive devotion.
rows.anchor: الخ، مفصولا إشعار بالعلية وذلك يؤيد ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly good granted to Abraham was a good life: he had abundant wealth and great moral nobility.
rows.anchor: الحسنة هي المعيشة الحسنة فقد كان عليه السلام ذا مال كثير ومروة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For fuller explanations, he directs readers to his discussions of choosing in Joseph, guidance and the straight path in al-Fātiḥa, and Abraham’s being among the righteous in al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: وقد بسطنا الكلام في معنى الاجتباء في تفسير سورة يوسف عند الآية 6

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s described qualities are gifts of the upright religion; whoever follows it is led to the same destination as Abraham.
rows.anchor: وفي توصيفه تعالى إبراهيم عليه السلام بما وصفه من الصفات إشارة إلى أنها من مواهب هذا الدين الحنيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating that Abraham was upright and not an idolater underscores these qualities for special emphasis.
rows.anchor: تكرار اتصافه بالحنف ونفي الشرك لمزيد العناية به

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: The lexicon derives sabt from cutting and gives examples such as stopping a journey, shaving hair, and cutting off a nose; sabt can also mean entering or observing Saturday.
rows.anchor: أصل السبت القطع ومنه سبت السير قطعه وسبت شعره حلقه، وأنفه اصطلمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One etymology says Saturday was named because God began creating the heavens and earth on Sunday, completed them in six days, and stopped work on Saturday.
rows.anchor: وقيل سمي يوم السبت لأن الله تعالى ابتدأ بخلق السماوات والأرض يوم الأحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrases about the Sabbath are explained as cutting off work, while not keeping the Sabbath means not stopping work or not being in the Sabbath; both describe the same state.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه لا يقطعون العمل وقيل يوم لا يكونون في السبت

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Sleep is called sabāt because it cuts off work, corresponding to the night’s purpose of giving people rest.
rows.anchor: أي قطعا للعمل وذلك إشارة إلى ما قال في صفة الليل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Anas says God accepts a person’s testimony when an ummah testifies for him; ummah can mean one person or more, as in the verse about Abraham.
rows.anchor: ما من عبد يشهد له أمة إلا قبل الله شهادتهم، والأمة الرجل فما فوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that his earlier discussion of verses about testimony is relevant to the report.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير آيات الشهادة ما له تعلق بالحديث

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Samaʿa ibn Mihrān reports the Imam’s view that Abraham was once the world’s only worshipper of Allah; if another had existed, the verse would have included him, then Allah comforted Abraham with Ishmael and Isaac, making three. The author notes a parallel al-Kāfī report from a righteous servant.
rows.anchor: لقد كانت الدنيا وما كان فيها إلا واحد يعبد الله ولو كان معه غيره لأضافه إليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Muslim community comes last historically but first on Judgment Day; Friday was prescribed to earlier scriptural communities, but after they differed Allah guided Muslims to it, with Jews and Christians following on later days.
rows.anchor: نحن الآخرون السابقون يوم القيامة بيد أنهم أوتوا الكتاب من قبلنا وأوتيناه من بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says similar versions are reported by Aḥmad and Muslim from Abū Hurayra and Ḥudhayfa, but the report was not transmitted as an explanation of this verse.
rows.anchor: ولم ترد الرواية في تفسير الآية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abū Laylā al-Ashʿarī reports the Prophet commanding obedience to the imams, equating their obedience and disobedience with obedience and disobedience to God; the Prophet’s mission is to call by wisdom and good exhortation, and those who oppose him are doomed. A leader who acts otherwise incurs the curse of God, angels, and all people.
rows.anchor: تمسكوا بطاعة أئمتكم ولا تخالفوهم فإن طاعتهم طاعة الله ومعصيتهم معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah chiefly warns: its stories end with the destruction of tyrants and deniers, its arguments press people toward monotheism and accepting truth, and it concludes with Judgment’s terrors and the ruin of criminals and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: تغلب فيها آيات الإنذار والتخويف على آيات التبشير غلبة واضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening consoles the Prophet: the Quran is a divine reminder, not a burden to force on people; his duty is to convey it, while hearers who fail to remember face destruction or return to God for the consequences of their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فليس عليه إلا التبليغ فحسب فإن خشوا وتذكروا وإلا غشيتهم غاشية عذاب الاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah appears Meccan; reports place either 20:130 or 20:131 in Medina, but the wording gives no evidence for either report.
rows.anchor: ولا دليل على شيء من ذلك من ناحية اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the declaration that Allah alone is God and possesses the most beautiful names one of the surah’s outstanding verses.
rows.anchor: الله لا إله إلا هو له الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭā Hā consists of two disconnected letters, like the other letter combinations opening Quranic surahs; he postpones discussion of reported interpretations to the later reports section.
rows.anchor: طه حرفان من الحروف المقطعة افتتحت بهما السورة كسائر الحروف المقطعة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes afterlife and worldly misery, with worldly misery divided into psychological, bodily, and external forms; he relays the view that misery can mean toil, though all misery is toil but not all toil is misery.
rows.anchor: والشقاوة كالسعادة من حيث الإضافة فكما أن السعادة في الأصل ضربان سعادة أخروية وسعادة دنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, the verse means that the Quran was not sent down to make the Prophet toil by straining himself to compel people to accept it.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى ما أنزلنا القرآن لتتعب نفسك في سبيل تبليغه بالتكلف في حمل الناس عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from a truth is called forgetting by a deliberate extension because both have the same effect: failing to attend to it.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي نسيانا بنوع من العناية وهو اشتراكهما في الأثر وهو عدم الاعتناء بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear of the consequences of heedlessness and indulging worldly desire is needed to jolt the soul toward truth, allowing the reminder to benefit its hearer.
rows.anchor: فلا بد في دفع هذا النسيان الذي أوجبه اتباع الهوى والانكباب على الدنيا من أمر ينتزع النفس انتزاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear are people disposed to respond: when they hear truth, latent fear appears, so they believe and become mindful.
rows.anchor: وأن المراد بمن يخشى من كان في طبعه ذلك، بأن كان مستعدا لظهور الخشية في قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: the Quran was not sent to burden the Prophet but to serve as a reminder that leads those inclined to fear toward belief and piety.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتتعب به نفسك ولكن ليكون مذكرا يتذكر به من شأنه أن يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, tadhkira is an active verbal noun and the purpose of the sending; tanzīlan is a passive verbal noun used circumstantially for the pronoun referring to the Quran, meaning a divine revelation that reminds the fearful.
rows.anchor: مصدرا بمعنى الفاعل ومفعولا له لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿulyā is the feminine plural of aʿlā, like fuḍlā from afḍal.
rows.anchor: العلى جمع عليا مؤنث أعلى كفضلي وفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the Creator of earth and the high heavens fits revelation as a descent from a source above to a destination below; what lies between is omitted because it is irrelevant here, unlike the ownership statement that stresses comprehensiveness.
rows.anchor: وقد خصصا بالذكر دون ما بينهما إذ لا غرض يتعلق بما بينهما وإنما الغرض بيان مبدأ التنزيل ومنتهاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the All-Merciful settled over the Throne begins a four-verse exposition of lordship, the core aim of the call and reminder.
rows.anchor: استئناف يذكر فيه مسأله توحيد الربوبية التي هي مخ الغرض من الدعوة والتذكرة وذلك في أربع آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Settling over the Throne is a metaphor for encompassing sovereignty and taking charge of affairs; for Allah it means His dominion appears across creation through management and ordering. It entails rule over every thing, great or small, and establishes Him as the sole Lord, since a lord owns and manages.
rows.anchor: الاستواء على العرش كناية عن الاحتواء على الملك والأخذ بزمام تدبير الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses following the Throne statement mention Allah’s ownership and knowledge as an argument explaining that sovereignty.
rows.anchor: ولذلك عقب حديث الاستواء على العرش بحديث ملكه لكل شي وعلمه بكل شي وذلك في معنى التعليل والاحتجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is an intensive form of mercy, which means effusion through creating and managing; its sense of abundance makes it especially apt with the Throne statement.
rows.anchor: وهو مبالغة من الرحمة التي هي الإفاضة بالإيجاد والتدبير وهو يفيد الكثرة أنسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax makes al-Raḥmān the subject, istawā its predicate, and ʿalā al-ʿarsh dependent on istawā; other verses use the same Throne formulation.
rows.anchor: أن { الرحمن } مبتدأ خبره { استوى } و { على العرش } متعلق بقوله { استوى }

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: He rejects an alternative parse that makes al-Raḥmān the subject with ʿalā al-ʿarsh as predicate, and treats istawā as a verb whose subject is what is in the heavens and whose object is all things belonging to Allah and obeying His will.
rows.anchor: أن قوله { الرحمن على العرش } مبتدأ وخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refers readers to his extended discussion of the Throne in his commentary on 7:54 and says a later report section will add material relevant here.
rows.anchor: وقد أشبعنا الكلام في معنى العرش في ذيل الآية 54 من سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Al-tharā is said to mean either moist soil or soil generally; what is beneath it is the earth’s interior, while what is on its surface and its known or unknown living things fall under what is in the earth.
rows.anchor: الثرى على ما قيل هو التراب الرطب أو مطلق التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the ownership covers everything within the heavens and earth, it also covers the heavens and earth themselves, which consist of their parts; this verse establishes ownership, one pillar of lordship.
rows.anchor: وإذا عم الملك ما في السماوات والأرض ومن ذلك أجزاؤهما عم نفس السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahr is speaking aloud, while isrār is its opposite; sirr is speech kept within oneself, and akhfā is a superlative meaning more hidden, not a past-tense verb with Allah as subject. Its indefinite form intensifies concealment.
rows.anchor: أفعل التفضيل من الخفاء على ما يعطيه سياق الترقي في الآية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: He rejects the view that akhfā is a past-tense verb meaning Allah knows the secret and what He has hidden.
rows.anchor: ولا يصغى إلى قول من قال إن { أخفى } فعل ماض فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moving from audible speech to the inner secret and then what is still more hidden proves Allah knows everything, even an intention concealed from its own thinker.
rows.anchor: وذكر الجهر بالقول في الآية أولا ثم إثبات العلم بما هو أدق منه وهو السر والترقي إلى أخفى يدل على أن المراد إثبات العلم بالجميع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes sirr as speech whispered to someone else and akhfā as a thought in the mind; the author accepts the account of whispering but says speech is secret only when kept within oneself.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بالسر ما أسررته من القول إلى غيرك ولم ترفع صوتك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s compact structure states Allah knows the secret and what is more hidden, which also answers whether He knows what is spoken aloud: if He knows the more hidden, He certainly knows the audible.
rows.anchor: فدل على الجواب في شقي الترديد معا وعلى معنى الأولوية بأوجز بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes Allah’s knowledge of everything visible and hidden, paralleling the statement that He knows what enters and leaves the earth after settling over the Throne.
rows.anchor: فالآية تثبت علمه تعالى بكل شيء ظاهر أو خفي فهي في ذكر العلم عقيب الاستواء على العرش نظيرة قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of events within Allah’s kingdom entails His approval and permission; from another angle it reflects His will for the existing order, which is governance. Verse 20:7 thus establishes universal management, while 20:6 establishes universal ownership; together they prove absolute lordship.
rows.anchor: فالآية تثبت عموم التدبير كما أن الآية السابقة كانت تثبت عموم الملك ومجموع مدلوليهما هو الملك والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He finds an omitted-subject parse contextually apt: the statement means that the one described in the preceding verses is Allah, with no deity but Him and the most beautiful names belonging to Him.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كان الأنسب أن يكون اسم الجلالة خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف والتقدير هذا المذكور في الآيات السابقة هو الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the verse considered as a self-contained unit, he gives another parse: Allah is the subject, no deity but Him is its predicate, and to Him belong the most beautiful names is a second predicate.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الأقرب بالنظر إلى استقلال الآية وجامعيتها في مضمونها أن يكون اسم الجلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of Allah’s sole divinity can be grounded in the preceding proof of His exclusive lordship or in the following statement that He possesses the beautiful names.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يعلل بما ثبت في الآيات السابقة من توحده تعالى بالربوبية المطلقة ويمكن أن يعلل بقوله بعده { له الأسماء الحسنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether ilāh means an object of worship or one truly worthy of worship, worship expresses servitude and dependence; its object must own and manage the worshipper, so Allah, the sole Lord of all, alone is worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: وإذ كان تعالى رب كل شيء لا رب سواه فهو المعبود لا معبود سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is motivated by hope for the worshipped one’s good, fear of harm from neglecting Him, or recognition that He deserves worship and submission.
rows.anchor: العبادة لأحد ثلاث خصال إما رجاء لما عند المعبود من الخير
